name: MonarchCurrencyInput
title: CurrencyInput
wrapsNative: TextField(value:format:) with FloatingPointFormatStyle<Double>.Currency and .keyboardType(.decimalPad), through MonarchNumberInput
summary: An amount of money in one currency, typed and shown in the person's locale with the currency's own number of decimals.
whenToUse: For a price, payment, budget or refund amount in a known currency, in major units (19.99) or in whole minor units (1999 cents).
whenNotToUse: Not for showing an amount that is not edited (use MonarchMoney), and not for a plain number or percentage (use MonarchNumberInput).
api: init(_ label: String, value: Binding<Double?>, currencyCode: String, currencyDisplay: MonarchMoneyCurrencyDisplay = .symbol, minimum: Double? = nil, maximum: Double? = nil, step: Double = 1, allowsNegative: Bool = false, prompt: String? = nil, helper: String? = nil, error: String? = nil, showsStepper: Bool = false, rangeMessage: String? = nil, isRequired: Bool = false, labels: MonarchFormFieldLabels = MonarchFormFieldLabels())

init(_ label: String, minorUnits: Binding<Int?>, currencyCode: String, currencyDisplay: MonarchMoneyCurrencyDisplay = .symbol, minimum: Int? = nil, maximum: Int? = nil, step: Int? = nil, allowsNegative: Bool = false, prompt: String? = nil, helper: String? = nil, error: String? = nil, showsStepper: Bool = false, rangeMessage: String? = nil, isRequired: Bool = false, labels: MonarchFormFieldLabels = MonarchFormFieldLabels())

options.name: value / minorUnits
options.description: The amount in major units, or in whole minor units for APIs that store integers. nil while the field is empty.

options.name: currencyCode
options.description: The ISO 4217 code, such as USD, EUR, JPY or KWD. Sets the symbol and the decimals (JPY 0, USD 2, KWD 3).

options.name: currencyDisplay
options.description: How the currency is written: symbol ($ or US$), narrowSymbol ($), code (USD) or name.

options.name: minimum
options.description: The smallest amount. Without it the smallest is 0, unless allowsNegative. Below it the range message is shown.

options.name: step
options.description: The amount one press of the stepper adds or removes.

options.name: allowsNegative
options.description: Allows amounts below zero, for refunds and adjustments.

options.name: prompt
options.description: Placeholder text while the field is empty.

options.name: error
options.description: An error message. Replaces the help text and the range message.

options.name: showsStepper
options.description: Shows the system Stepper beside the field. Amounts are usually typed.

options.name: rangeMessage
options.description: Replaces the built-in message for an amount outside the bounds.

options.name: isRequired
options.description: Shows a mark after the label and adds "Required" to the hint.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the spoken "Required" and the form of an error.

states.name: empty
states.description: The prompt is shown and the value is nil.

states.name: filled
states.description: The amount is written in the locale's currency format with the currency's decimals.

states.name: out of range
states.description: Below the minimum (zero by default) or above the maximum: the danger border and a message such as "Enter a number of at least $0.00".

states.name: error
states.description: The danger border and the app's message with an icon, announced.

states.name: disabled
states.description: With .disabled(true): the disabled fill and text roles; the field and stepper cannot be used.

appearance: The MonarchNumberInput field: surface fill, input border, focus ring, tabular digits; the danger strong role for errors and the disabled roles when disabled. Every colour is a theme role, so dark and high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: Formatting and parsing are the system's currency format style, applied with the environment's locale, so the separators and symbol position follow the person's region like the web's Intl formatting. A typed amount is rounded to the currency's decimals when it is committed (on submit or when the field loses focus), as on the web. iOS has no large step (Page Up and Page Down); the stepper is the system Stepper and is off by default, as on the web. The minor-units initialiser converts through Decimal, so 19.99 dollars is exactly 1999 cents.
accessibility: The field is one element labelled with label, whose value is the formatted amount with its currency and whose hint is the error ("Error: …") or the help text.
A new error or range message is announced.
The number keyboard is the decimal pad, or the keyboard with a minus sign when negative amounts are allowed.
The field is at least 44 points high and its text scales with Dynamic Type; errors have an icon and text, not colour alone.
edgeCases: Text that does not read as an amount leaves the value unchanged, as the system TextField(value:format:) does.
1.005 with USD is rounded to 1.01 (half away from zero on the decimal text, not the binary double).
An unknown currency code is formatted with 2 decimals, the system's default.
A value below zero is kept and flagged when negative amounts are not allowed; it is not silently changed.

examples.title: Minor units (cents)
examples.template:
MonarchCurrencyInput(
    {{label}},
    minorUnits: $cents,
    currencyCode: {{currency}},
    helper: "Stored as \(cents ?? 0) cents."
)
.environment(\.locale, Locale(identifier: "en_US"))
examples.code:
MonarchCurrencyInput(
    "Unit price",
    minorUnits: $cents,
    currencyCode: "USD",
    helper: "Stored as \(cents ?? 0) cents."
)
.environment(\.locale, Locale(identifier: "en_US"))
